[Capacity]{.eyebrow}

## Training and capacity building

A core aim of the project is to build a lasting network of African modellers, with capacity building embedded in how the project works day to day:

- **At each hub** — learning by doing, on real decision problems.
- **Across hubs** — teams working jointly and sharing methods.
- **Across the ecosystem** — knowledge sharing and cross-learning with partners and programmes.

Hands-on training runs across the hubs in Tanzania, the DRC and Nigeria, pairing early-career researchers with experienced modellers.

[Open challenges]{.eyebrow}

## Hackathons and modelling competitions

The network runs hackathons and modelling competitions — open challenges that grow skills, surface new approaches, and connect modellers across countries and disciplines.

[Community]{.eyebrow}

## A Community of Practice

MoDD Africa contributes to a regional **Community of Practice (CoP)** in vector epidemiology and modelling, a space to share methods, data and lessons and to keep the ecosystem connected as it grows.

[Programmes]{.eyebrow}

## For national malaria programmes

We work directly with National Malaria Programmes to make sure models answer the questions that matter for control and elimination — and that the outputs are usable where decisions are made.

[Careers]{.eyebrow}

## Opportunities

Research and PhD positions open periodically through the Ifakara Health Institute. See current openings on the [IHI jobs board](https://www.ihi.or.tz/our-job-posts/), or get in touch via the [Contact](contact.qmd) page.
